note:
These are the estimates selected by World History Encyclopedia’s reviewed secondary account, not established census totals: around 40,000 Byzantine and allied troops versus 20,000–25,000 Rashidun troops. The Rashidun midpoint is used for display. Medieval accounts disagree substantially. The source calls roughly 4,000 Rashidun losses casualties; they are not relabeled as deaths. It provides no comparable numeric Byzantine loss total. Equipment remains unclassified pending dated evidence.

The Byzantine side uses an explicitly representative early Byzantine spear-and-large-shield infantry component. Procopius attests the equipment family; sixth–seventh-century segmented helmets and the military prescriptions of the Strategikon supply the period analogy. This is not direct evidence of the equipment worn by every soldier at Yarmouk, the share of infantry, allied contingents, or a uniform. Rashidun equipment remains unclassified: the checked narrative mentions swords but does not establish a sufficiently specific complete equipment silhouette. Strength and loss estimates are unchanged. This reviewed assignment supersedes the earlier blanket note that both sides have unclassified equipment.
